Retain the baseline before reviewing a candidate. Follow comparison and export to complete the loop without losing the evidence behind a change.

title: Connect a PyTorch loop
summary: Use table views, weighted samplers and explicit metric passes with an existing PyTorch model.
text: Granum can sit around an ordinary PyTorch training loop. A table view loads or transforms a sample; a sampler chooses training examples; a separate collection pass records model behaviour against the canonical inputs. Prepare data Create a table , then define a module-level transform for the format your model expects. A training transform may augment inputs. A metric transform should return a dictionary and keep the source labels and identity meaningful. from torch.utils.data import DataLoader import granum # load_training_sample is your module-level transform. view = train_table.with_transform(load_training_sample) loader = DataLoader(view, batch_size=32, sampler=granum.create_weighted_sampler(train_table)) Do not combine a sampler with shuffle=True . For multiple worker processes, the transform must be picklable. Keep a separate clean evaluation view instead of measuring randomly augmented training samples as though they were canonical observations. Record training and evaluation Start a run with granum.init , store your recipe in parameters , and log aggregate scalars with granum.log . At the intended intervals, use collect_metrics with a task-appropriate collector and Predictor(model, preprocess=...) . Include the split and epoch. Predictor supports model device placement, evaluation mode and optional layer hooks. Resolve layer indices against model.named_modules() when collecting activations; they are not permanent layer names across different architectures. Remove hooks when the predictor is no longer needed. Inspect and iterate Open the run to confirm input joins, labels and predictions before a long training session. Freeze the input table URLs in the run parameters. After editing labels, create a new dataset version and start a new experiment so the comparison retains both inputs. The repository's CIFAR-10 and detection examples provide concrete loops. The recipe catalogue lists what is included. Automatic conversion of an arbitrary PyTorch Dataset object is Not yet included ; use explicit rows or a TableWriter to preserve the fields and identity you intend to analyse.

title: Connect YOLO training
summary: Collect predictions and per-sample metrics from Ultralytics detection, mask, pose and rotated-box runs.
text: Use the Ultralytics integration when you already train a compatible YOLO model. Granum records the experiment and collects predictions against the registered tables. The dashboard training flow is covered in Train a model . Prepare compatible data Load the exact training and evaluation tables and export them to the task layout your model needs. Use detect , segment , pose or obb consistently between import, export and the model. Confirm class names and original image sizes before attaching callbacks. import granum from granum.integration.ultralytics import add_granum_callback granum.export_yolo({"train": train_table, "val": valid_table}, "out/yolo", task="detect", image_strategy="copy") add_granum_callback(model, {"train": train_table, "val": valid_table}, project_name="inspection", run_name="baseline", collect_every=1, track_learning=True) model.train(data="out/yolo/data.yaml", epochs=10) This fragment assumes an instantiated compatible model and loaded table variables. Start with a short run to verify the data and prediction contract before extending it. Choose collection frequency collect_every controls collection intervals; recording every epoch enables finer learning dynamics and recurring label findings at additional inference and storage cost. final_only can reserve a named split for the final collection instead of exposing it to routine inspection each epoch. Predicted geometry retains task information: masks for segmentation, landmarks for pose, corners for oriented boxes. Matching follows the task's mask IoU, OKS or rotated IoU rather than replacing all geometry with an ordinary bounding box. Existing model checks collect_detection_metrics(model, table, run=..., split=...) supports a prediction pass without training a new model. Inspect unknown-class handling and thresholds. A model trained on a different class vocabulary cannot judge labels it does not understand. Current boundary A dedicated YOLO classification callback and the legacy standalone YOLOv5 repository adapter are Not yet included . Classification can use the generic PyTorch metrics contract . GPU, model-version and customer-dataset qualification remain specific to the environment used.

title: Connect Hugging Face
summary: Preserve sample identity through Datasets and collect Trainer predictions or hidden-state embeddings.
text: Use the Hugging Face adapter with a configured Trainer, Dataset preprocessing and Granum collectors. From a source checkout, install the huggingface extra in your selected Python environment. Keep model-specific tokenisation and image processing in your own pipeline. Build an indexed dataset from granum.integration.hugging_face import to_dataset, collect_predictions from granum.metrics import ClassificationMetricsCollector dataset = to_dataset(table, columns=["features", "label"]) dataset = dataset.shuffle(seed=7).select(range(min(100, len(dataset)))) result = collect_predictions( trainer, table, dataset, [ClassificationMetricsCollector(classes=classes)], run=run, split="validation", epoch=1, ) The fragment assumes table , trainer , classes and run already exist and the selected fields match your model. Preserve both __granum_* identity columns through preprocessing. The integration removes identity fields from the copy passed to the model while keeping them for joins. A dataset from another table revision is rejected. Attach training collection GranumTrainer accepts granum_run and a mapping of granum_evaluations built with Evaluation . It logs aggregate measurements and runs prediction collection after evaluations. collect_every controls frequency. The caller remains responsible for finishing the Granum Run. For hidden states or nonstandard outputs, supply prediction_transform to return a Granum Prediction(outputs, activations) . It receives the complete Hugging Face prediction result, not only logits. Restore image geometry to source coordinates and semantic masks to source resolution. Verify the joins Check a shuffled subset and confirm the joined source records before running a full dataset. This is especially important after tokenisation, filtering or image preprocessing. Do not recreate IDs from the final row positions. Single-process Trainer prediction, embeddings and training callbacks have development verification. Distributed use requires calling collection on all ranks, with the world process zero writing, but broader distributed and task-specific vision qualification remains open. Ready-made recipes for individual text and segmentation models are Not yet included .

title: Connect Lightning
summary: Record validation and test outputs from Lightning while preserving source sample identities.
text: The Lightning callback collects per-sample outputs during validation and test. Install the lightning extra from your source checkout and configure your usual Lightning model and Trainer. Prepare indexed inputs from granum.integration.lightning import IndexedDataset, Evaluation, GranumCallback # load_sample_dict returns a dictionary suited to your model. eval_dataset = IndexedDataset(valid_table.with_transform(load_sample_dict)) callback = GranumCallback( run, validation=[Evaluation(valid_table, collectors, "val")], test=[Evaluation(test_table, test_collectors, "test")], ) Pass this dataset through an appropriate DataLoader and include the callback when constructing the Lightning Trainer. The transform returns a dictionary, and the collator must retain the added identity fields. Those fields allow collection to match outputs to source samples even when loader order changes. Return model observations Validation and test steps can return a logits tensor, a dictionary containing logits , or a Granum Prediction . Use output_transform(outputs, batch) when your module returns a different structure. Preserve one output per identified sample. Model geometry must map back to source coordinates before vision collectors evaluate it. Sanity-validation passes are skipped. collect_every sets the interval, and close_run=True opts into callback management of completion or failure. Otherwise, finish the Run in your own process. Check distributed behaviour The callback gathers distributed measurements and removes sampler-padding duplicates only when repeated metrics agree. Conflicting observations for one sample are an error rather than an arbitrary choice of one value. This matters when stochastic transforms are accidentally left in evaluation. Development checks include real CPU fit/test and two-process CPU/Gloo validation. GPU training and other distributed strategies still require qualification for the intended environment. Run a small known dataset and check counts and joins before scaling. Continue the workflow Open the run, inspect the source images and confirm epoch labels. Use per-sample learning for repeated observations and comparison when evaluating a candidate. A packaged Lightning semantic-model tutorial is Not yet included ; the callback's generic output contract is available for your own model pipeline.

title: Connect Detectron2
summary: Register Granum tables and collect detection, instance-mask or keypoint predictions with a Detectron2 evaluator.
text: The Detectron2 integration exposes tables through its dataset catalogue and records predictions with GranumEvaluator . Install Detectron2 for your chosen PyTorch, compiler and CUDA environment before using this optional adapter. Register a dataset from granum.integration.detectron2 import register_dataset, GranumEvaluator from detectron2.evaluation import inference_on_dataset register_dataset("granum_validation", table) evaluator = GranumEvaluator(table, run=run, task="segment", split="val", epoch=0) summary = inference_on_dataset(model, validation_loader, evaluator) Here validation_loader must be built from the registered dataset using your Detectron2 loader configuration. Its mapper must preserve image_id and __granum_table_url . Use the task matching your table and model: detection, instance segmentation or pose. Preserve annotation meaning Category IDs are mapped to contiguous model classes and mapped back when recording metrics. Check class names rather than assuming dataset IDs already match model output positions. For bitmap masks, configure cfg.INPUT.MASK_FORMAT = "bitmask" . The adapter handles the COCO/Detectron2 half-pixel keypoint convention. Avoid applying that conversion a second time in a custom mapper. Keep source image dimensions so predictions can be related to original geometry. Integrate with training Return a GranumEvaluator from your DefaultTrainer.build_evaluator override or combine it with another evaluator. iteration=lambda: trainer.iter can record the active training step. Keep the Run available across evaluations and finish it when the training process concludes. Verify a small shuffled evaluation set and inspect joined predictions before extending training. Development evidence includes the real dataset catalogue/mapper, class and keypoint mapping, Mask R-CNN optimisation and inference on CPU. Not yet included Rotated-box input is refused by this adapter. Dedicated semantic/panoptic adapters, embedding hooks and qualified distributed/GPU workflows are not yet included. Use the YOLO OBB path for supported rotated-box work, or the custom collector contract for an explicit model-output adapter.

title: Connect SuperGradients
summary: Collect indexed evaluation results and canonical YOLO-NAS detection or pose predictions.
text: Use a separate Python environment for SuperGradients. The verified development combination uses SuperGradients 3.7.1 on Python 3.10 with PyTorch 2.5.1 CPU, torchvision 0.20.1 and setuptools 66.1.1. Its dependency constraints differ from the main development environment; installing every framework into one environment can produce incompatible packages. Preserve sample identity from granum.integration.super_gradients import ( IndexedDataset, identity_collate, Evaluation, GranumCallback, ) from torch.utils.data import DataLoader dataset = IndexedDataset(table.with_transform(load_sample)) loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=16, collate_fn=identity_collate) callback = GranumCallback(run, validation=[Evaluation(table, collectors, "val")]) load_sample returns (inputs, target) and may include a third extras dictionary. Add the callback to the Trainer's phase_callbacks and use the indexed loader for the corresponding evaluation. For variable-size detection targets, IdentityCollate(DetectionCollateFN()) preserves the source fields around the native collation function. Adapt predictions An evaluation's output_transform can convert the framework result into collector inputs. Return Prediction(outputs, activations) to include embeddings. Restore predicted geometry to the original image coordinates before comparing it with canonical labels. SuperGradientsPredictor provides a separate prediction pass for YOLO-NAS detection and pose using the model's configured processing pipeline. Supply it through an Evaluation predictor_factory . Class vocabulary, pose layout and preprocessing still need to match the registered table. Verify the run Check a shuffled subset, sample counts and a few image overlays. Development checks include real two-epoch Trainer fitting, validation/test joins, embeddings, variable-target collation and actual YOLO-NAS detection/pose prediction pipelines. Random-weight inference confirms integration behaviour, not model accuracy. Not yet included Full native YOLO-NAS training recipes, ready-made detection/pose Table transforms and qualified GPU/distributed workflows are not yet included. Supply your model's transforms explicitly and validate them on a small dataset. The recipe catalogue records these gaps without presenting a partially configured Trainer as a complete tutorial.

title: Use Granum from Python
summary: The same objects the app uses, for scripted imports, custom metrics and your own training loop.
text: Everything the dashboard does sits on a small Python API, and the app is a client of it like any other. Use it when your work is repetitive, when your training loop is your own, or when the metric you care about is not one Granum computes. import granum from granum import Table granum.set_config(granum.Config.load(overrides={"project-root-url": "~/granum"})) table = Table.from_coco("data/train/_annotations.coco.json", "data/train", project_name="aerial", dataset_name="human_aerial", table_name="train") print(len(table), table.columns) Tables A Table is one version of one set: rows of samples, a schema that knows what each column means, and a parent. Editing returns a new table rather than changing this one. fixed = table.apply_edits(values={"bbs": {4172: corrected_boxes}}) # a new version subset = table.filter(lambda row: row["bbs"]["instances"]) # images with labels latest = table.latest() # newest safe revision Runs and metrics run = granum.init("aerial", "baseline", parameters={"framework": "yolo", "epochs": 12}) from granum.metrics import DetectionMetricsCollector for epoch in range(12): ... # your training loop granum.log({"epoch": epoch, "map50": score}, run=run) granum.collect_metrics( valid, [DetectionMetricsCollector("bbs", value_map=valid.schema["bbs"].value_map)], predictor=my_predictor, constants={"epoch": epoch}, split="valid", ) collect_metrics writes one metrics table per call, joined by the input table reference and sample ID, with the predicted boxes and per-image counts the dashboard reads. Anything you collect this way appears in the app: the run views, per-image learning and — when the predictions are stored every round — Findings. Training and export from granum import export_yolo export_yolo({"train": train, "val": valid}, "/tmp/export", image_strategy="symlink") The bundled trainer is a module, so a scripted run is one command: python -m granum.training.train --project-root ~/granum --project aerial \ --train-table URL --valid-table URL --run-name nightly \ --family yolo --version yolo26m.pt --epochs 30 --track-learning The service API The dashboard talks to the REST service, and so can you — /api/projects , /api/images , /api/run/findings , /api/runs/compare and the rest. Default local mode accepts loopback peers and checks Host, Origin and paths. Shared mode adds authenticated HTTPS and workspace-wide roles. Inspect the live request schema at /docs on your running service. Continue with the SDK Use tables , schemas , transforms , runs and custom collectors for complete examples. The Python API reference and service API map are available on this site. Framework-specific guides are in Connect your training code .

title: Create and revise tables
summary: Construct datasets, read rows and bulk data, and keep subsets and edits as traceable revisions.
text: granum.Table represents one persisted dataset revision. Choose a table constructor for a known format or create typed columns explicitly. Configure the project root before writing data; the examples below use the active configuration. Create and load from granum import Table from granum.schemas import Float32Schema, StringSchema table = Table.from_dict_data( {"sample": ["a", "b", "c"], "score": [0.2, 0.8, 0.5]}, schema={"sample": StringSchema(), "score": Float32Schema()}, project_name="table-demo", dataset_name="train", ) loaded = Table.from_url(table.url) assert len(loaded) == 3 print(loaded[0]) from_pandas , from_parquet , from_csv , from_image_folder , from_coco , from_yolo_url and from_semantic_masks provide other constructors. CSV fields begin as strings; explicitly convert them if the intended values are numeric. Read samples and bulk data table[index] reads a sample according to each column's schema. to_arrow() exposes the backing Arrow table, to_pydict() returns columns, and to_pandas() converts to a DataFrame. These bulk operations can materialise the dataset in memory. A large dataset is not automatically a streaming iterator merely because it uses Parquet storage. Image schemas can return a stored URL or decoded PIL image. Use transforms for model-specific preprocessing without rewriting the original table. Make revisions set_values , set_weights , add_column , delete_columns , delete_rows and apply_edits return new tables. Keep the returned object or URL. parent , children , siblings , descendants , lineage and depth expose history. latest() follows the safe revision path; ambiguous branches need an explicit selection. Pin a URL for reproducible training instead of resolving latest during every epoch. Subsets and new data filter(predicate) creates a persisted subset. subset(include_probability=..., seed=...) samples a row range. join_tables(other) appends compatible rows and records both parents; it is not a relational key-based join. Check schema/class-map compatibility and duplicate media before combining. The dashboard's pull from projects workflow adds preflight and review. Write rows and batches TableWriter(schema=..., project_name=..., dataset_name=...) accepts add_row , add_batch or extend , then finalize() writes a table. Declare all required fields; weights can default to 1. The writer currently accumulates data in memory. External bulk-array storage and a plugin sample-type registry are Not yet included .

title: Define column schemas
summary: Give values their types, display meaning and edit rules before storing them in a table.
text: Schemas describe stored values and how Granum should interpret them. Use explicit schemas when a number represents a class, weight, probability or sample reference; inference cannot reliably infer that meaning from its magnitude. Core schema families Import these types from granum.schemas . Family Types Scalar values BoolSchema , Int32Schema , Int64Schema , Float32Schema , StringSchema , UrlSchema Measurements ConfidenceSchema , FractionSchema , ProbabilitySchema , IoUSchema Sample and run context SampleWeightSchema , ExampleIdSchema , EpochSchema , ForeignTableIdSchema Categories CategoricalLabelSchema , CategoricalLabelListSchema , ValueMapEntry Media and vectors ImageSchema , VideoUrlSchema , EmbeddingSchema , Int32ListSchema Geometry and tables Geometry2DSchema , BoundingBoxes2DSchema , TableSchema A video URL column stores a reference; it does not provide the reserved video ingestion/timeline workflow. Likewise, an embedding column describes vectors, not a point-cloud annotation type. Declare categories and geometry from granum.schemas import BoundingBoxes2DSchema, CategoricalLabelSchema label = CategoricalLabelSchema(classes=["acceptable", "defect"]) boxes = BoundingBoxes2DSchema( classes=["part"], instance_properties={"confidence": "float32", "source": "string"}, ) A value map associates stable integer IDs with names and display information. Do not silently reuse an ID for another class. Geometry instance properties must be declared with a supported type; undeclared fields are rejected. Vision importers preserve masks, keypoints and rotated geometry in the appropriate annotation representation. Configure display and access Column metadata includes description , writable , default_visible and number_role . Metrics should not become editable ground truth merely because they look like a label column. Some context columns identify source tables, rows and epochs for joining; keep them distinct from user annotations. ImageSchema(sample_type="url") returns a location. The pil_png , pil_jpeg and pil_webp modes load referenced images through Pillow; writing a PIL object directly is not supported. EmbeddingSchema(shape=(128,)) declares a vector's intended width. Projection also validates actual row dimensions and numeric values. Validate a small sample Write a few rows, reload them, inspect the Arrow schema and open them in the dashboard. Catch class-map, coordinate and type mistakes before importing a large collection. User-defined external sample types and arbitrary bulk-array adapters are Not yet included .

title: Transform samples on read
summary: Use different training and evaluation views while keeping one immutable source table.
text: table.with_transform(function) returns a TableView . It applies a function whenever a sample is read and leaves the stored table unchanged. Use it for decoding, normalisation and model input preparation. Make a read view from granum import Table table = Table.from_dict_data( {"signal": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]}, project_name="transform-demo", dataset_name="samples", ) def scale(sample): return {**sample, "signal": sample["signal"] / 3.0} view = table.with_transform(scale) assert view[0]["signal"] != table[0]["signal"] The returned values are transient. To preserve a derived measurement, explicitly write a typed column in a new revision. To preserve augmented images/annotations as a dataset, use versioned augmentation . Use with a training loader A model-training view can return whatever sample structure its loader expects. With multiple worker processes, use a picklable module-level function and handle platform multiprocessing requirements. Keep random seeds and augmentation settings with the run parameters. The metrics collection path requires a dictionary per sample so collectors can address columns by name. It also needs predictions aligned with the canonical input labels. Do not reuse a randomly cropped or shuffled training view without a clear identity and coordinate-restoration contract. Keep geometry consistent A spatial transform must update every affected annotation: boxes, masks, oriented corners and keypoints. A horizontal pose flip also needs a landmark swap mapping. Cropping an image while leaving its boxes in the old coordinates creates invalid evaluation evidence. Use model adapters that restore predictions to original-image coordinates, or do that restoration explicitly before a collector receives them. Semantic prediction masks must match the source resolution. Limits and next steps TableView is a Python read-time view, not a materialised browser subset or a new dataset revision. A public custom sample-type/plugin registration system and automatic logging of every randomly augmented training observation are Not yet included . See extensions and the reserved recipes .

title: Manage runs in Python
summary: Record parameters, aggregate metrics and sample observations with explicit experiment lifecycle.
text: A Run groups one experiment's recipe, status and measurements. Create a new run when changing data, model settings or evaluation rules that need to remain distinguishable in a comparison. Start and finish import granum run = granum.init( "run-demo", "baseline", parameters={"seed": 7, "learning_rate": 0.001}, constants={"purpose": "smoke-check"}, if_exists="raise", ) run.log({"epoch": 0, "train_loss": 0.72}) run.set_status("finished") print(run.url) The example numbers are illustrative API inputs, not measured model results. In a real process, record actual scalars and set failure/cancellation status when appropriate. Creating a Run does not start a training worker. Handle names deliberately init defaults to if_exists="rename" , which chooses an unused name. raise refuses a collision; reuse opens an existing run. overwrite removes the existing run at that location and should only be used when replacing that history is intended. init also sets the active Run. granum.log and collect_metrics can use it implicitly, but explicit run=... is clearer when managing multiple experiments. get_active_run and set_active_run control that context. Reload a recorded run with Run.from_url . Add measurements Use run.log or granum.log for aggregate scalars. Use collect_metrics , Run.add_metrics or MetricsTableWriter for sample-level data. Manual metrics need the correct input table reference and sample IDs; the writer cannot infer how an arbitrary external loader reordered outputs. metrics_tables() returns the stored sample tables. join_input() on one metrics table combines its measurements with the corresponding input rows. aggregate_metrics() reads the scalar history, and joined() provides run-level joined data subject to its options. Record the recipe Save the source table URLs, preprocessing, class order, seed, thresholds, model weights and hyperparameters needed to repeat the result. set_parameters updates the parameter record but is not an independent hyperparameter-search scheduler. Managed sweeps and compute queues are Not yet included . Open the run in the dashboard and confirm joins before using learning dynamics or comparison .

title: Write custom collectors
summary: Record your own measurements or embeddings with a consistent per-sample output contract.
text: A collector receives a batch of source columns and optional predictions. It returns a dictionary of metric names to equally sized lists. Every output position must describe the corresponding input sample. Granum handles batching, input IDs and persistence around that contract. A complete model-free example import granum from granum.metrics import FunctionalMetricsCollector from granum.schemas import Float32Schema table = granum.Table.from_dict_data( {"value": [1.0, -2.0, 3.0]}, project_name="collector-demo", dataset_name="samples", ) run = granum.init("collector-demo", "absolute-values") collector = FunctionalMetricsCollector( lambda batch, prediction: {"magnitude": [abs(v) for v in batch["value"]]}, column_schemas={"magnitude": Float32Schema()}, ) metrics = granum.collect_metrics(table, [collector], run=run, constants={"epoch": 0}) assert metrics.to_pydict()["magnitude"] == [1.0, 2.0, 3.0] run.set_status("finished") The callback does not require a model. Use this pattern for an image statistic, external quality score or domain-specific measurement. For per-object statistics, declare typed properties on the geometry rather than confusing one object value with one image value. Adapt model output Wrap a model with Predictor or supply a compatible callable. Prediction carries outputs and a mapping of activation layers. Keep labels, class order, geometry coordinates and array dimensions consistent with the chosen collector. Subclass MetricsCollector when a functional wrapper is insufficient. Implement collect and column_schemas . Collector names must not collide with reserved identity fields or with other collectors in the same call. Missing columns or unequal lengths are refused to prevent corrupted joins. Collect embeddings EmbeddingsMetricsCollector(layer=..., column="embedding", reshape="mean") reads a captured layer. Configure the same layer index on Predictor(layers=[...]) . Mean pooling reduces spatial dimensions; flattening keeps them and can greatly increase storage. A callable can implement model-specific pooling. Verify one vector per sample before projection . Aggregate without losing meaning MeanAggregator , SumAggregator , MinAggregator , MaxAggregator and aggregate_metrics_table provide explicit aggregation. Choose a statistic suited to the metric. For example, averaging per-image IoU is different from summing class intersections and unions before calculating IoU. Keep the underlying sample measurements so the aggregate can be investigated later.

title: Storage paths and caches
summary: Understand object directories, URL aliases, cloud access, row caches and saved projections.
text: Granum separates table metadata from referenced media. A project's records can remain small while its images live elsewhere, but portability requires preserving or relocating those references. Object layout A table URL names its directory, not the JSON file inside it: <project-root>/projects/<project>/ datasets/<dataset>/tables/<table>/ object.granum.json row_cache.parquet runs/<run>/ object.granum.json metrics_0000/ ProjectLayout resolves these locations. Additional records track imports, review, releases, views and other project state. Treat metadata and Parquet payloads as a unit; do not rename individual object files to move a table. Use supported project and backup operations. URLs and aliases Url handles local paths and fsspec-backed locations. Its path joining and read/write methods use the selected filesystem. Install the corresponding cloud extra and configure credentials on the machine doing the reading. import granum granum.register_url_alias("IMAGES", "/data/images") location = granum.Url("<IMAGES>/sample.png") print(location.resolved) print(granum.get_registered_url_aliases()) Aliases let a process resolve a logical root to its local storage location. Register matching aliases wherever you use the data; a Python-only alias does not automatically configure a separately running service. GRANUM_ALIAS_<TOKEN> is the environment form. Conflicting aliases need explicit resolution. Row caches and indexing The Parquet row cache is the backing data used by to_arrow() and sample reads. Do not delete it as though it were a disposable thumbnail. The table.row-cache configuration entry exists, but cacheless reconstruction is Not yet included in the current table read path. The object index discovers records beneath configured roots, watches changes and exposes projects, tables and runs. A forced reindex can discover new records; it cannot repair missing source payloads. See service operation . Saved projections Reducer.save preserves a fitted coordinate system. Reducer.load restores it; nonlinear reducer loading requires trusted=True because its serialised model can contain executable pickle state. Load only artifacts from a trusted source. Reuse requires the same embedding model and preprocessing, not merely equal vector width. External chunked array/geometry storage and custom adapter registration are Not yet included . Cloud media also has separate deployment and backup boundaries .

title: Python API reference
summary: Find Granum public objects, constructors, metrics, configuration and integration entry points.
text: The Python package is imported as granum . The reference below groups its current public entry points by task. Use the linked guides for complete workflows and the installed symbol's docstring for the signature in your exact build. Granum is an alpha package; pin its revision with your environment. Top level objects Symbol Purpose Table , TableView Persisted dataset revisions and read-time transformations TableWriter , MetricsTableWriter Construct table or metrics rows/batches and finalise them Run , MetricsTable Experiment records and measurements linked to input samples Config , get_config , set_config Resolve and select process configuration Index , get_index , set_index Discover and resolve project objects ProjectLayout , Url , load_object Object locations, filesystem access and object loading BoundingBoxes2D , box_iou , match_boxes , nms Detection geometry and matching utilities schemas , metrics , __version__ Typed-column/measurement namespaces and package version Table constructors and access Call Behaviour Table.from_dict_data(data, schema=None, *, project_name=..., dataset_name=...) Create a table from equally sized columns Table.from_pandas(df, **kwargs) Convert a DataFrame Table.from_parquet(url, **kwargs) Read Parquet columns Table.from_csv(url, **kwargs) Read CSV fields as strings Table.from_image_folder(root, **kwargs) Register class-directory images Table.from_coco(annotations, image_folder=None, **kwargs) Read COCO annotations and referenced media Table.from_yolo_url(data_yaml, split="train", *, task=None, **kwargs) Read one YOLO split and task Table.from_semantic_masks(manifest, **kwargs) Read lossless class-ID mask data Table.from_url(url) / Table.from_names(project_name, dataset_name, table_name) Load an exact revision table[index] , to_arrow() , to_pydict() , to_pandas() , summary(column) Sample, bulk and summary access See tables for revision methods, subsets, append operations and lineage. See schemas for scalar, categorical, vector, media and geometry types. Run and metric functions init(project_name, run_name, *, parameters, constants, if_exists, config) creates a Run; log(values, *, run=None) records aggregates. get_active_run and set_active_run control implicit run selection. Run methods include set_parameters , set_status , add_metrics , metrics_tables , aggregate_metrics and joined . A MetricsTable exposes input_table , join_input and to_pandas_joined . collect_metrics(table, metrics_collectors, *, predictor=None, model=None, run=None, split=None, constants=None, batch_size=32, exclude_zero_weights=False, column_schemas=None, description="") returns a persisted MetricsTable. Each collector must produce one output per sample. The granum.metrics namespace exposes Prediction , Predictor , MetricsCollector , FunctionalMetricsCollector , ClassificationMetricsCollector , DetectionMetricsCollector , SemanticMetricsCollector and EmbeddingsMetricsCollector . It also includes iter_batches , Aggregator , MeanAggregator , SumAggregator , MinAggregator , MaxAggregator , aggregate_metrics_table , DynamicsThresholds , compute_dynamics , epoch_summary and training_dynamics . Read metrics and collectors before providing custom model outputs. Sampling export and reduction create_weighted_sampler , create_random_sampler , create_sequential_sampler and create_repeat_by_weight_sampler operate on table weights. See weight semantics . export_coco , export_yolo and export_semantic_masks write supported interchange formats. Select an explicit task and image strategy appropriate to the destination. granum.reduction provides Reducer , methods , reduce_table and reduce_run ; see projections . Configuration and integrations register_url_alias , unregister_url_alias and get_registered_url_aliases manage process URL aliases. Config.load(overrides=..., config_file=..., use_config_files=..., use_env=...) resolves settings. Read configuration before changing the root of an existing service. Framework modules are granum.integration.ultralytics , hugging_face , lightning , detectron2 , super_gradients , rfdetr and sam . Use the framework guides for dependency and output contracts. A module's presence does not imply every model family/task combination is supported. Errors and extension boundaries Top-level errors include GranumError , TableError , SchemaError , ConfigError , RunError , ImmutableError , ObjectNotFoundError and AliasConflictError . Metrics adds CollectionError , CollectorError and PredictorError . Keep the original error when reporting a failed operation. A public compute-plugin SDK, arbitrary sample-type registry and third-party URL-adapter registration are Not yet included . Internal helpers are not interchangeable with a supported plugin contract.

title: Run the Granum service
summary: Serve the dashboard, discover projects and inspect background jobs from one workspace service.
text: The Granum service reads project records, supplies media and metrics to the dashboard, and supervises supported jobs. The default deployment is on the same machine as the browser or desktop window. Start locally granum --project-root-url ~/granum service --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --open Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 for the application. The interactive service API reference is at /docs on that address; it is separate from this public product documentation. /api/health reports the running build and defensive limits, while /api/access identifies the access mode. granum open --browser starts or opens the local app flow. On a configured Linux desktop install, granum app status reports the background service. Use the foreground terminal when running a manual development service rather than assuming it belongs to systemd. Discover projects The index scans configured locations for Granum object directories. Watch mode and scan interval control discovery; CLI flags include --watch / --no-watch and --scan-interval . When a new Python process writes a table to the same root, it should become visible through the index. If a table is missing, compare the writer's root with the service root, then check aliases, permissions and the object's metadata/payload. POST /api/reindex refreshes discovery. Reindexing does not reconstruct missing row data or move images into the project. Jobs and recovery Imports, projections, training and related work expose job status through /api/jobs/{id} . Read the phase, progress and error before repeating a request. Cancellation is explicit and can wait for a calculation boundary. Supervised training processes can outlive a service restart, and the service reconnects to them. A dead trainer may be marked interrupted. Do not interpret a closed browser as a cancelled job or start a duplicate training process without checking status. Shared access Local mode rejects non-loopback peers. For team access, use the authenticated shared-workspace setup with HTTPS. Changing only the bind host is insufficient. Use configuration for roots and network settings and operations for backup, audit and recovery procedures.

title: Configure a workspace
summary: Resolve settings, environment variables, data roots and service options in a predictable order.
text: Configuration controls where Granum stores records and which resources its service may read. Confirm the resolved settings before creating data or pointing a second process at an existing workspace. Inspect effective values granum config show granum config path granum config validate Resolution proceeds from defaults through system, user and project configuration, then environment variables, then explicit overrides. config show reports provenance so an unexpected environment variable can be distinguished from a saved file. Global CLI options precede the subcommand. Settings reference Setting Environment variable Default or meaning project-root-url GRANUM_PROJECT_ROOT_URL ~/granum ; project record root service.port GRANUM_SERVICE_PORT 8000 service.data-roots GRANUM_SERVICE_DATA_ROOTS Import roots; platform path separator between roots service.allowed-origins GRANUM_SERVICE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Additional browser origins, comma-separated indexing.scan-interval GRANUM_INDEXING_SCAN_INTERVAL 10 seconds table.row-cache GRANUM_TABLE_ROW_CACHE true ; current reads require the persisted row cache display-progress GRANUM_DISPLAY_PROGRESS true log-level GRANUM_LOG_LEVEL WARNING log-file GRANUM_LOG_FILE Empty unless configured licence.server GRANUM_LICENCE_SERVER Legacy licence service location; current alpha enforcement is disabled Do not disable the row-cache setting expecting automatic reconstruction; that path is Not yet included . Set the storage location A YAML configuration can include: project-root-url: /srv/granum service: port: 8000 data-roots: /srv/datasets Changing the project root selects another location; it does not migrate existing records or media. Restart a long-running service when changing the environment it inherited. CLI --data-root can be repeated; --allow-host and --allow-origin serve different purposes from authentication. Configure Python separately import granum config = granum.Config.load(overrides={"project-root-url": "/tmp/granum-example"}) granum.set_config(config) Python overrides affect that process. They do not modify an already running service's configuration. Use URL aliases for logical media roots and shared access for authentication/TLS. File locations vary by platform; see Files and settings .

title: Share a workspace with a team
summary: Provision authenticated HTTPS access and understand the workspace-wide roles.
text: Shared mode lets several people use one Granum service with authenticated accounts. All accounts can read every project, media item, run and job exposed by that service. Use separate services/workspaces when those readers must not have access to the same data. Provision accounts and HTTPS Run account provisioning on the service host. The following paths and hostname are examples to replace with administrator-controlled locations for your installation: granum access add-user admin --role admin --file /secure/granum-users.json granum access add-user reviewer --role reviewer --file /secure/granum-users.json granum --project-root-url /srv/granum service --host 0.0.0.0 --auth-file /secure/granum-users.json --tls-cert /secure/granum-cert.pem --tls-key /secure/granum-key.pem --allow-host granum.example.org Passwords are entered through the hidden prompt; the registry stores salted hashes. Keep the registry and private key outside data roots and project backups. Use a certificate trusted by clients. Shared HTTP Basic authentication requires HTTPS; unsupported non-loopback startup fails closed. Choose a role Role Scope Viewer Read accessible workspace data and use supported read-only analysis Annotator Add annotation changes, comments, tags, views and exploratory versions Reviewer Also perform reviews, approval, recoverable curation and supported model/analysis jobs Administrator Full service management, including destructive and installation operations Shared writes derive the author from the authenticated account. A typed reviewer name in local mode does not provide that same authentication. Changes and revocations in the registry require a service restart; check existing jobs separately. Collaborate without losing edits A stale base revision is rejected instead of silently overwriting another user's saved work. Retain your draft, open the latest data and reconcile explicitly. Sharing an analysis workflow JSON transfers view settings, while a shared service gives access to the actual workspace. Read operations for audit-write failures, browser recovery and portable backups. A filesystem administrator remains trusted; the logs are not tamper-proof attestations. Not yet included Managed organisation accounts, granular per-project permissions, SAML/OIDC SSO, Azure Entra ID login, API-key management and multi-tenant isolation are not yet included. Their scope is reserved under enterprise identity . Existing role-based shared access does not provide those capabilities.

title: Use cloud storage
summary: Access S3, Google Cloud Storage or Azure-backed data while keeping credentials and concurrency boundaries explicit.
text: Granum's URL layer uses fsspec to access supported filesystems. Cloud storage can hold project records or referenced media when the required backend and credentials exist in the process reading them. A cloud root does not create a managed Granum service. Install the storage backend From a source checkout, install the extra for your provider: python -m pip install -e ".[service,images,s3]" Use gcs or azure in place of s3 for those providers. Configure credentials through your provider's normal environment or machine identity. A desktop browser's cloud login is not automatically available to a Python service or remote trainer. Configure a root granum --project-root-url s3://your-bucket/granum service Replace the example bucket and prefix with an accessible location. gs:// and az:// are corresponding provider-backed URL schemes. Confirm read/write permissions and test a small dataset before storing important project records there. All processes must resolve referenced media consistently; aliases can help when local and remote paths differ. Serve media The service checks media references and reads through its configured storage access. Granum currently does not provide a browser-direct signed cloud-media URL workflow. That optimisation is Not yet included ; see enterprise deployment . Keep credentials on the service side and limit accessible roots to the intended data. Concurrency and backup Local writer locks and atomic publication do not establish distributed locking semantics for object stores or network filesystems. Simultaneous multi-machine writes to a cloud/NFS workspace are Not yet included as a supported deployment. Use a single controlled writer path or a local service root while qualifying the actual storage environment. Portable backup refuses unsupported cloud media and external cross-project dependencies. Materialise required resources locally before using that workflow; provider storage snapshots have their own consistency and restore requirements. See operations . Remote training A remote trainer needs the same logical data, compatible Granum installation and its own credentials. It also needs a deliberate way to make the resulting records visible to the service. Managed remote job orchestration is reserved in remote environments .

title: Remote and container environments
summary: Plan remote data access and find the current boundary for notebooks, containers and managed training.
text: Granum can be run from a Python environment on another machine, but that machine's filesystem, credentials and network addresses are separate from those of your browser. Start by deciding where project records, source media, model weights and the service will live. Supported building blocks Use the service on the machine that can read the data. Connect a browser through an intentionally configured shared HTTPS deployment . A training process uses its configured project root and supported framework integration . A browser URL containing localhost addresses the browser's machine. A remote service also cannot read a dataset merely because it exists on the laptop showing the dashboard. Check the data path from the service and trainer independently. Cloud-backed URLs can help share data locations, subject to the cloud storage limits . Use consistent class maps, aliases and source revisions on both machines. A local metadata copy must still reference media that exists at the resolved destination. Docker and Kubernetes Not yet included. There is no qualified container image, Compose stack, Helm chart or Kubernetes operator supplied as a complete Granum deployment. This section is reserved for persistent volumes, service identity, TLS, GPU access, health checks, upgrade/rollback and single-writer rules. Running Python in a container yourself does not establish those operational guarantees. Retain the same service access checks and explicitly mount the records and media your workload requires. Hosted notebooks Not yet included. Turnkey Google Colab and AWS SageMaker connection guides, managed tunnels and persistent notebook lifecycle integration are reserved. The Python SDK can be installed in a compatible environment, but temporary notebook disks, browser reachability and disappearing processes remain your environment's responsibilities. Remote jobs Not yet included. Managed worker registration, remote queues, scheduling and resource assignment are reserved under compute . A dashboard training job currently runs through the configured service's supervised model process. Starting it does not schedule an independent cloud training fleet. For the supported local deployment, follow the guided course . Qualify a custom remote setup on a separate workspace before transferring the only copy of a project.

title: Operate a pilot workspace
summary: Approval, browser recovery, authenticated shared access, audit failures, integrity checks, portable backups and safe upgrade rehearsal.
headings: Handle an audit failure without duplicating work
text: This guide is for the person responsible for keeping a pilot workspace usable and recoverable. For a worked example with real results, follow the aerial course , especially review/recovery , approval/export and backup/restore . Approval is an explicit gate Creating a dataset version—entire dataset or verified subset—creates an exploratory version. Use Datasets → Approve… → Check and approve to approve exact contents. Every included image must have matching review evidence for its row, schema and media bytes. Empty sets, stale reviews, duplicate image references, missing media and changed contents can fail the gate. Approved-only training validates release membership and approval in both the service and the training process. Exploratory dashboard training requires acknowledgement. Direct SDK callers remain trusted and may deliberately explore; approval is not a blanket ban on all unapproved Python experiments. Approval records review evidence, not objective label truth. It checks media at approval/startup, not continuously for the entire run. Protect media against external writers. Local logs are unsigned and filesystem administrators can modify them; this is not tamper-proof attestation. Browser recovery and stale saves The annotation editor and review inspector store recovery copies in IndexedDB . Wait for the storage acknowledgement. Recover in the same browser profile and origin; a new port, desktop profile or private session may have different storage. A matching base can be recovered; a different base disables automatic replay. On conflict, retain/export the draft, open the latest revision and reconcile explicitly. Server save failure keeps the draft. A confirmed server commit is not undone merely because browser cleanup failed; read the separate warning before retrying. Export drafts before clearing site data, reinstalling a browser profile or abandoning a failed save. Browser drafts contain potentially sensitive annotations/comments. They are not server backups or cross-device synchronization. The service rejects stale shared commits. Identical supported commit retries reuse the committed child revision; arbitrary manual retries after an ambiguous failure still require state inspection. Local mode versus shared mode Default local mode accepts loopback peers only. Host, Origin and path checks are defence in depth, not a login system. Local author names are self-reported and local filesystem users are trusted. Shared mode is one whole workspace . Every account can read every project, media item, run and job visible to that service. There is no per-project access isolation, SSO, managed hosting or user-assignment system. Use separate workspaces/services if datasets must not be visible to the same readers. Role Writes allowed Viewer None; read-only analysis requests remain available Annotator Annotation commits, comments, tags, saved views and exploratory versions Reviewer Annotator actions plus review/approval, recoverable curation and supported training/analysis jobs Administrator All routes, including management, installation and permanent deletion Shared requests derive authors from the authenticated account, overriding submitted names. Do not equate this with protection against an administrator who directly edits filesystem records. Provision shared access deliberately Keep the account registry and TLS private key outside all project/media scan roots and backups . Use a certificate trusted by clients and restrict network exposure with a firewall or VPN. The following uses illustrative administrator-owned paths and a hostname you must replace with your actual setup. granum access add-user admin --role admin --file /secure/granum-users.json granum access add-user reviewer --role reviewer --file /secure/granum-users.json granum --project-root-url /srv/granum service --host 0.0.0.0 \ --auth-file /secure/granum-users.json \ --tls-cert /secure/granum-cert.pem --tls-key /secure/granum-key.pem \ --allow-host granum.example.org Passwords are prompted invisibly and stored as salted scrypt hashes. Never put them in command-line arguments, URLs, source files or support chat. HTTP Basic credentials must travel over HTTPS . Non-loopback startup without the required authentication/TLS fails closed. A loopback backend behind a trusted TLS proxy must not also be exposed as unauthenticated HTTP; forwarded headers are trusted only from loopback. POSIX registry files must be owner-only; on Windows use appropriate NTFS permissions. Account changes and revocations require a service restart. A browser may cache Basic credentials; closing its window is not administrative revocation. Review or cancel already-running jobs separately. Handle an audit failure without duplicating work Shared mutations append request and completion records to the workspace audit log. If the request cannot be recorded, mutation is refused. If completion logging fails after a change was committed, the service preserves the real result, returns a warning/request identifier and blocks subsequent writes. Retain the error, request ID and operation details. Inspect project state to determine whether the operation committed. Preserve the audit log; do not delete it to clear the warning. Repair the storage/permission problem and restart the service. Reconcile an interrupted request with no completion record before deciding whether to retry. The log does not include credentials, but it can contain sensitive project/operation information. Back it up separately with suitable permissions; it is not a cryptographically signed record. Media integrity and portable backup Stop service, model jobs and other project/media writers before a snapshot. Use a destination outside the source project. The following is the same workflow used in the course, with generic project names: granum --project-root-url /srv/granum integrity snapshot my-project --output /backups/media.json granum integrity verify /backups/media.json granum --project-root-url /srv/granum backup create my-project --output /backups/my-project.zip granum --project-root-url /srv/granum-rehearsal backup restore /backups/my-project.zip --name restored-check Integrity verification reports changed/missing bytes without replacing them. Baseline manifests are not overwritten. Portable backup includes supported local project records, local referenced media and recorded weights. Restore validates checksums/names/sizes in staging, relocates supported references and refuses an existing target. Limits include 200,000 files , a 32 MiB manifest and a default 100 GiB expanded restore ; --max-gib can raise the last limit. Large Parquet relocation can require substantial RAM. Cloud media and external table/cross-project dependencies must be materialised first or backup is refused. Archives are not encrypted. A project archive is not a complete system backup: separately protect app artifacts, Python/CUDA environments, relevant external outputs, training caches, browser drafts, workspace audit logs and credentials. Preserve access controls when transferring backups. Rehearse an upgrade and rollback Retain the current application artifact, its build identity and an offline project snapshot. Restore into a disposable separate root with the candidate build. Verify media hashes, images, reviews, release contents and run/weight references. Test read/edit/recovery and intended approval/training selection there—not on the only original. Keep the original unchanged as rollback until qualification is complete. Future object formats are refused explicitly. Do not assume an older application can read records written by a newer one; no universal automatic in-place schema migration is promised. Unusual non-media path fields may require re-review after relocation. Know the qualification boundary Local writer locks and atomic publication are not distributed locks for cloud stores, NFS or network shares. Interrupted-record tests do not emulate every filesystem, disk controller or power loss. Some large operations remain materialising rather than streaming; consult measured limits . The course demonstrates a small Linux source workflow, real YOLO GPU jobs and one local restore. Qualify your exact installer, OS, GPU, storage, access setup and workload before promising them to a pilot.

title: Upgrade and migrate safely
summary: Keep a recoverable workspace while changing Granum builds, dependencies or storage locations.
text: An upgrade changes the program reading and writing your project records. Record the old and new build identities, retain the prior artifact and verify the candidate against a restored workspace before replacing your working installation. Rehearse the upgrade Finish or deliberately stop writers and model jobs. Confirm their final status. Create a portable backup and keep any external resources it does not contain. Restore into a different project root using the candidate build. Inspect images, labels, reviews, dataset versions, runs and weight references. Exercise one edit/save/reopen and the intended approval/training path. Keep the original workspace and application artifact until the new environment is accepted. Do not point an older build at the only workspace already modified by a newer build and assume it will understand every format. Unsupported future object formats are explicitly refused. Move a workspace Changing project-root-url selects another root; it does not copy or rewrite project records. Use the supported backup/restore path for portable local moves. URL aliases can relocate logical media roots, but the actual bytes must still be present and accessible. Compare integrity manifests after a move. Browser recovery drafts and saved workflow preferences belong to the browser profile/origin and do not automatically move with the server's project directory. Export the drafts and workflow JSON you need separately. Dependency changes Pin the model environment as well as Granum. Framework versions, CUDA runtime, model weights and preprocessing can affect outputs even when the dataset is unchanged. A package version of 0.1.0 alone is not enough to identify a development build; retain the source revision/build manifest. Not yet included A universal automatic schema migrator, migration tool for another product's native object format, and a complete historical version-to-version compatibility matrix are not yet included. Exchange supported datasets through COCO, YOLO or other formats , then recheck labels and splits. Product-specific history and metrics require an explicit conversion contract. Read release information and current feature availability when choosing a candidate build.

title: Advanced analysis extensions
summary: Reserved space for additional operators, derived views, component plots and retrieval analysis.
text: Not yet included. The capabilities below have reserved documentation sections. Current calculations , charts and workflows remain available within their documented scope. Additional calculation operators Not yet included: a complete array/text/time/geometry expression catalogue. Reserved families include array indexing and unrolling, vector sorting/median/uniqueness, vector normalisation, string parsing and word counts, filename extraction, datetime components, hashes, constants, general boolean composition and arbitrary nested-property extraction. Also reserved are general binning, threshold clustering, traversal ordering, nearest-neighbour links, group-neighbour links, link-distance operations and automatic category encodings. The image duplicate workflow has its own neighbour analysis; it does not expose all these as general column operators. Ordered scalar differences are available. A full vector derivative/deviation and chained reduction operator library remains reserved. Geometry area/volume/line/triangle calculations and general cross-geometry matching expressions need explicit data contracts before their reference can be added. Additional plot and view types Not yet included: a guided N-component/parallel-coordinate chart, dedicated reduced-table tabs, dynamically reduced charts and arbitrary multi-table/multi-run view composition. A reduced table would group rows by chosen keys and materialise aggregate measurements. This is different from reducing the dimensions of embeddings, which is already available. For now, use explicit Python aggregation to create a new typed table, the existing linked scatter/image charts, or the supported two-run comparison screen. A general saved subset-tab interface is also reserved; persisted Python subsets and dashboard dataset versions are available alternatives. Retrieval and cross table analysis Not yet included: question-to-chunk and chunk-to-question relationships, retrieval candidate links, before/after semantic matches, embedding-distance comparisons, semantic similarity changes, selection-relative chunk relationships and interactive foreign-table operations. Run metrics already join to their registered input samples. That specific join does not provide a general foreign-table query language, edited-row relationships or a retrieval evaluation product. This section will need a worked question/document dataset, identity rules and interpretation of retrieval scores before it can become a usage guide. Sampling and selection Not yet included: optimised weighted coreset selection, persisted 3D volume selection and a general multi-column travel-distance wizard. Use weight-aware samplers , explicitly saved subsets and the documented screen-space 3D selection behaviour today. Each future guide will identify its inputs, calculation scope, saved output and missing-value rules. No release date or executable interface is implied by these reserved sections.

title: Managed compute and plugins
summary: Reserved space for a compute service, plugin catalogue and automated model workflows.
text: Not yet included. Granum has local model jobs, optional training support and Python integrations. A managed compute platform and public plugin system are planned separately from those existing paths. Compute service Reserved capabilities include worker registration, resource selection, remote queues, scheduling, retry rules, job ownership and environment isolation. A complete guide will explain how a request moves from the dashboard to a worker and how results are attached to exact data versions. Today, use service-supervised jobs and inspect their logs and status. A local training process continuing after a service restart does not imply remote scheduling or cluster failover. Plugin SDK and catalogue Not yet included: a public plugin manifest, compute interface, UI contribution contract, package builder, version-compatibility rules and a trusted plugin catalogue. There is no supported install, update or uninstall flow for arbitrary community compute plugins. This section reserves space for plugin authoring, private catalogue registration, environment health, logs, dependency resolution and installation policies. When implemented, it will include one complete plugin and its test/deployment procedure. Granum's current training add-on is an existing dependency installation path, not a general plugin marketplace. Automatic labelling pipelines Not yet included: unattended dataset-wide SAM segmentation, model-assisted active-labelling queues, automatic dataset-growth schedules and a built-in pipeline for training crop classifiers then attaching per-instance embeddings. Use Pre-label for supported model drafts and SAM for interactive image-level proposals. Review suggestions, create a new dataset version, train and compare explicitly. These manual stages preserve an inspectable record while the orchestration is reserved. Hyperparameter jobs Not yet included: a managed sweep scheduler with resource budgets and automatic candidate selection. Runs already store hyperparameters, metrics and the source versions used. You can run your own experiment driver and attach each result through Python runs . The future compute guides will document cancellation, resource limits, recovery and credential scope alongside launch instructions. Until those contracts exist, this page deliberately supplies no placeholder CLI commands or configuration keys.

title: Enterprise identity and delivery
summary: Reserved enterprise account, SSO, access-isolation and media-delivery capabilities.
text: Not yet included. The sections below describe intended enterprise capabilities. The current single-workspace shared mode already provides authenticated HTTPS and roles; these reserved capabilities require additional implementation. Organisation accounts and API keys Managed account signup, organisation membership, workspace invitations, service accounts, scoped API keys and key rotation are not yet included. Existing shared accounts are provisioned on the service host and have workspace-wide visibility. Current unrestricted-alpha builds need no in-app licence activation. This does not create a managed account platform or self-service paid subscription. See access and licensing for the behaviour of the current build. Single sign on Not yet included: SAML or OIDC single sign-on, Azure Entra ID setup, identity-provider group mapping, just-in-time account provisioning and central session revocation. The future guide will contain supported protocols, callback configuration, certificate/key rotation and a tested login/recovery flow. There are no supported Granum SSO environment variables to configure today. Access isolation Not yet included: per-project permissions, multi-tenant data isolation and organisation-wide assignment policies. All authenticated readers of one shared service can read that service's workspace. Separate services and roots remain the current way to keep reader populations apart. Signed media delivery Not yet included: browser-direct, self-authenticated cloud media URLs with bounded lifetime and provider permissions. Media currently follows the configured service access path. The future guide will need to explain URL lifetime, cache handling, revocation and the relationship to user access. Enterprise deployment lifecycle A separately qualified enterprise control plane, offline entitlement workflow, managed updates, central policy administration and enterprise support matrix are not yet included. Local/on-premise service operation and manually provisioned shared HTTPS are documented today. For present deployments, use operations for audit behaviour, backups, recovery and upgrade rehearsal. Existing audit records are unsigned and filesystem administrators remain trusted. Enterprise compliance claims are not implied by the availability of local logs.

title: Point clouds and 3D annotations
summary: Reserved ingestion, visualisation and editing for spatial datasets and synchronised sensors.
text: Not yet included. Granum does not currently provide a complete point-cloud data model, dedicated 3D annotation editor or sensor-sequence import workflow. Spatial data types This section is reserved for point clouds, meshes, three-dimensional points, lines and triangles, 3D bounding boxes/cuboids, coordinate frames, units and per-point or per-object attributes. A usable workflow must specify which coordinate system each label belongs to and how transformations affect it. Future type guides will include a small input, its schema, supported storage representation and a round-trip export check. They will distinguish geometric data from an embedding vector that happens to contain three numbers. Annotation and inspection Reserved editor capabilities include selecting points or volumes, placing and rotating cuboids, inspecting occlusion, linking cameras to spatial views and applying per-point labels. Their save, review and revision semantics need to be defined alongside their interaction controls. The current 3D scatter plot displays numeric observations and supports screen-space selection. It does not make this annotation workflow available. Its selection is based on projected centres at all depths, not a persisted spatial volume. Sensor datasets Not yet included: PandaSet ingestion, synchronised camera/LiDAR views, multi-sensor calibration, point-cloud sequence playback and a worked autonomous-driving example. The reserved guide will need to preserve sequence identity, timestamps, calibration and train/evaluation grouping. For externally prepared image-only portions, supported image imports remain available. Keep their sequence and sensor metadata so the reduction to images is explicit; do not describe the result as a complete spatial dataset import. Current alternatives Keep spatial annotation in your existing tool, export the image or scalar measurements Granum can represent, and attach model observations through Python tables . Use linked identifiers if you need to trace results back to the original spatial record. This page will gain supported formats, import commands, editor examples and validation checks with the implementation. No point-cloud importer or 3D training API is being promised by the reserved page.

title: Custom data and storage extensions
summary: Reserved public extension contracts for sample types, bulk arrays, URL adapters and discovery.
text: Not yet included. Granum exposes typed tables, read-time transforms, collectors and fsspec-backed URLs. The extension systems below need additional public contracts before they can be documented as supported plugin interfaces. Custom sample types Reserved capabilities include user-defined external and inline sample types, acceptance/type detection, custom serialisation, source-URL resolution and plugin registration. Built-in image URL/PIL reads and TableView transformations remain available. For now, store supported scalar/vector/media fields and decode them in your own transform. Keep unsupported payloads outside the table and retain an explicit reference. A Python class existing in your process does not make it reloadable in a separate service or installed desktop build. Bulk array and geometry storage Not yet included: a public external-array store, inline-to-external conversion policy, configurable chunked geometry/array storage and automatic bulk-data placement. TableWriter currently accumulates rows in memory, and table access relies on the persisted Parquet payload. The bulk_data directory in the project layout is not itself a supported array-storage API. Define resource limits and a consistent reference contract before writing a custom pipeline around it. URL adapters and discovery Not yet included: a Granum-specific public adapter registration interface with declared read/write capabilities, precedence over built-in schemes, adapter-owned scan roots and custom discovery invalidation. Existing storage backends use fsspec and the documented cloud extras. Use URL aliases for relocating supported roots. Use an explicit reindex when records need discovery. Neither operation grants a new service permission or implements a new storage protocol. Import and export plugins Not yet included: a general importer/exporter registry for third-party packages and an arbitrary PyTorch Dataset converter. Use explicit TableWriter construction and the known exchange formats , then validate class maps, sample IDs and media access. A separate compute-plugin SDK is also reserved. When these extension contracts are included, each will get an installable example, versioning rules, error behaviour and a round-trip validation procedure. Internal helper functions are not presented here as stable plugin APIs.

summary: Every screen, what it is for, and what its controls do.
text: The sidebar provides project navigation and the available data, training and review screens. Some analysis views open from a dataset or run. Licence controls depend on the build's enforcement mode. Projects Every project on this machine as cards or a list, with a mosaic, its type and sets, counts, how much is verified, and the last run's status. Search, sort, and create a project. Rename and delete live here too. → Manage projects Overview One project at a glance: the data as a mosaic, headline numbers, the hardest sample from the last run, training progress, sample dynamics, and an Attention list of what Granum thinks needs looking at — import findings, unverified sets, runs that stopped. Images The main working screen, in three modes. Mode Turn on with For Browse default Looking: filters, ordering, annotations, the full-screen viewer → guide Review Review in the ribbon Verifying, rework, comments, isolate, delete → guide Edit Edit in the ribbon Drawing and correcting boxes, masks, keypoints → guide The image workflow also provides Create dataset , Removed , Pre-label , Duplicates , Stats and Fields . Follow duplicate inspection , draft labels and annotation tools for the full workflow. Table and run workspace Linked Rows, Filters and Charts expose the data behind a dataset or run. Calculate derives columns; Workflows saves analysis settings; Embeddings creates projections; Landmarks inspects pose properties. → Inspect tables and runs Health The dataset readiness view brings import, split, similarity, model-draft and review evidence together. Its specialised views depend on the task and stored predictions. → Inspect model errors Datasets The dataset versions created from Images — the only data training uses.
